turn1.explanation: The unit responds to frontal faces of small, furry, pointy-eared mammals: cats, foxes, red pandas and lynx most strongly, with hamsters, meerkats and ferrets as weaker related cases. Images built around other things push it negative, especially flat-faced or droopy-eared dogs (pugs, boxers, mastiffs), birds and hairless or smooth-skinned animals.
turn1.evidence: The top 20 are almost all cat, fox or red-panda faces with fluffy fur and upright ears; the one outlier is a red vintage car at #5, which may share the warm orange-red colour. The most negative images are dominated by pugs and mastiff-type dogs plus birds, a hairless dog, a buffalo and some objects, so it separates feline/vulpine faces from canine brachycephalic faces.
